{{alias}}( order, norm, uplo, diag, M, N, A, LDA, work )
    Computes a norm of a triangular or trapezoidal matrix.

    Upper matrices require M <= N; lower matrices require N <= M.
    Unit diagonal values and the opposite triangle are not referenced.
    Infinity workspace must contain M elements and must not overlap A.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string|integer
        Row-major or column-major storage layout.
    norm: string
        Norm name: 'max', 'one', 'infinity', or 'frobenius'.
    uplo: string|integer
        Upper or lower triangular storage.
    diag: string|integer
        Unit or non-unit diagonal.
    M: integer
        Number of rows.
    N: integer
        Number of columns.
    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix storage.
    LDA: integer
        Leading dimension.
    work: Float64Array
        Infinity norm workspace; ignored by other norms.

    Returns
    -------
    v: number
        Matrix norm.

    Examples
    --------
    > var values = [ 2, -3, 4, NaN, 5, -6 ];
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( values );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}( 101, 'infinity', 121, 131, 2, 3, A, 3, work )
    11


{{alias}}.ndarray( norm, uplo, diag, M, N, A, sa1, sa2, oa, work, sw, ow )
    Computes a matrix norm with explicit strides and offsets.

    Parameters
    ----------
    norm: string
        Norm name: 'max', 'one', 'infinity', or 'frobenius'.
    uplo: string|integer
        Upper or lower triangular storage.
    diag: string|integer
        Unit or non-unit diagonal.
    M: integer
        Number of rows.
    N: integer
        Number of columns.
    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix storage.
    sa1: integer
        Row stride.
    sa2: integer
        Column stride.
    oa: integer
        Matrix starting index.
    work: Float64Array
        Infinity norm workspace; ignored by other norms.
    sw: integer
        Nonzero workspace stride for the infinity norm.
    ow: integer
        Workspace starting index.

    Returns
    -------
    v: number
        Matrix norm.

    Examples
    --------
    > var values = [ -6, 5, NaN, 4, -3, 2 ];
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( values );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > var f = {{alias}}.ndarray;
    > f( 'infinity', 'upper', 'non-unit', 2, 3, A, -3, -1, 5, work, -1, 1 )
    11


    See Also
    --------
